svg.text: Deep dive 2 — consistency of matching: two invariants
drive side is horizontally scaled (many instances) → only a SHARED store can keep them in sync
Invariant 1 — one ride, one outstanding request (easy)
a single ride is handled by ONE matcher instance,
so a local while-loop is enough:
while not match:
next driver → notify → wait ~10 s → repeat
no shared state needed — per-instance loop satisfies it.
Invariant 2 — no driver gets two requests (hard)
concert lets out: 100k riders, same top-10 drivers.
Requests land on DIFFERENT matcher instances — each one
independently returns "driver 1 is closest".
Driver 1's phone: dzzz-dzzz-dzzz — 100 notifications.
Option A — status + cron (works, not great)
set driver.status = request_sent + updated_at;
cron resets stale request_sent → available.
downside: driver stays locked ≤ TTL + cron interval
(5 s + up to 60 s) — suboptimal during surges.
Option B — distributed lock with TTL (winner)
SET driver:{id} = true (Redis) · TTL 5 s
every instance checks the lock BEFORE notifying:
exists → skip to next driver. TTL expires on
no-response → auto-release. O(1) hashmap lookup.
Same trick as Ticketmaster's ticket lock — append this sentence in the interview:
"one shared store (Redis) gives every matcher instance a consistent global view of who is already occupied, and the TTL handles the driver who never answers."
